analysis.title: GS Financials & REITs Sector Specialist: Afternoon Update/Inbounds
key_insights: The most topical conversation among clients on 28 Oct 2026 is pain in capital markets, with a couple of unexplained price moves drawing attention (MRX named).

The top debate is where floor value sits on LPLA, which trades cheaper than regional banks, and how much of the recent move is positioning versus a changing fundamental view. The desk notes it is a tough tape in capital markets to go out and defend the stock.

Bulls like LPLA for its operational flexibility (cash) and for being a relative winner on competition. The change of course is that competition is now hitting net new assets (NNA), and clients are asking whether the stock can work without a clear catalyst, with NNA expected to be muted near term.

The desk says it is harder to be short LPLA unless a client wants to be short the whole group, given its relative valuation versus peers and the more low-growth, capital-intensive nature of those peers.
A couple of earnings misses are seeing continued follow-through selling and are starting to draw incremental client inbounds (SLM, BRO, HIG).
Senior housing is in focus. VTR is off its lows and some clients are coming around.

Other inbound topics: whether EVR is idiosyncratic or a bellwether for peers, and the ICE setup. Per the desk, more bulls ask why bears focus so much on mortgage than bears actually focused on mortgage.
Other inbound topics: weakness in regional banks today, and ESS setting a low bar, with the question of whether other REITs can miss on new leases and still work.
Other inbound topics: lab REITs, JVs and leverage, and ORCL implications for financials (CDS tightening on its funding message).
Other inbound topics: SPGI and the multiples that apply to its mortgage insurance (MI) business, and the bullish feedback on RNR and ACGL, or conversely what bears are scared of.

The desk lists Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research first takes published this morning on APAM, AON, BXP, ESS, EVR, EXR, JLL, LPLA, HOOD, RNR, V and VTR, with links only and no content in the text.
